messages:
jamie_smith: Heads-up — Valence Labs POC is getting intermittent SSE disconnects during large responses. Their client reports JSON parse errors from partial chunks. Happened twice during a 10m test. I pasted relevant logs below from their app and our gateway.

morgan_dev: thanks. do we know if it's through our hosted endpoint or their proxy?

jamie_smith: hitting hosted (api.redwood.ai) from their staging app in eu-west-1. They said it works sometimes, fails on long responses (~6-10KB).

rui_oncall: can you paste the raw response boundary log? also if they can repro w/ native EventSource that'd narrow sdk vs stream.

jamie_smith: here's the snippet they captured (client side):

```
EventSource onmessage chunk: "{\"items\":[{\"id\":\"r1\",\"text\":\"start...\"}, {\"id\":\"r2\",\"text\":\"mid"
SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
```

jamie_smith: and our gateway logs around the same time (correlation id 7f3c):

```
[2026-03-20T14:12:02Z] conn=abcd1234 recv: 1024 bytes
[2026-03-20T14:12:02Z] conn=abcd1234 send  chunk: 512 bytes
[2026-03-20T14:12:02Z] conn=abcd1234 send  chunk: 2048 bytes
[2026-03-20T14:12:05Z] conn=abcd1234 closed by server (code=1001) reason="timeout"
```

akshat_infra: interesting — server closed with 1001 (going away). Do we have proxy in front of the gateway? Nginx or cloud LB?

jamie_smith: customer uses a corporate proxy on their side, but request goes direct to hosted endpoint (no nginx on our end). They did mention occasional spikes in latency on their network.

morgan_dev: two likely buckets: (1) client-side parser sees chunk boundary inside JSON because the server sends a large event split across TCP chunks (this is normal) — the client must reassemble before JSON.parse; or (2) our runtime ended the connection early (keepalive/idle timeout or explicit close) causing truncated events. Need to confirm which.

rui_oncall: can we repro with a local script that subscribes with EventSource and logs raw data frames? Also check if the SDK does incremental JSON.parse (it should buffer).

jamie_smith: Valence tried with our JS SDK and with native EventSource. SDK sometimes shields it, but native EventSource reproduces the parse error reliably. They can repro by requesting a long completion with streaming=true and artificially slowing their network.

akshat_infra: ok. two debug steps to run now: 1) ask customer to capture full raw SSE stream (no SDK) and paste markers between 

---RAW START---
:heartbeat

data: {"items":[{"id":"r1","text":"start"},

data: {"items":[{"id":"r2","text":"mid"},

---RAW END---

akshat_infra: ^ that shows an extra `data:` starting mid-object — looks like their client or a proxy is splitting and preprending framing incorrectly. also check for any intermediate re-writes.

morgan_dev: Also check headers from our gateway when this happens: content-type should be `text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`, transfer-encoding chunked, and there should be no content-length. Any presence of `Connection: close` or a downstream `x-accel-buffering: no` would be relevant.

jamie_smith: pulled headers they saw: `content-type: text/event-stream;charset=utf-8`, `transfer-encoding: chunked`, `x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 27`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 42`. nothing obvious.

rui_oncall: what about TCP-level resets or an intermediate proxy doing buffering with chunk reassembly? Their corporate proxy sometimes breaks on long SSE sessions. Ask them to test against a simple `curl -N` to our endpoint from the same host — that'll show whether network/proxy is corrupting stream.

jamie_smith: they ran `curl -N` and saw the same broken boundaries when they route through their corporate proxy. Bypassing the proxy (dialing straight) makes it stable. Customer says they cannot remove the proxy long-term due to security policy.

akshat_infra: OK — this is starting to look like a corporate proxy that treats newline sequences as message delimiters and inserts `data:` markers or re-chunks in the middle of SSE events. Two mitigation options: 1) server-side: emit more frequent SSE comment-heartbeats and smaller event sizes so that proxies don't split inside JSON objects, or 2) client-side: modify parsing to buffer across `data:` lines and only JSON.parse once full object assembled (robust to split boundaries). We should propose both.

morgan_dev: quick patch we can ship to SDK: make the JS SDK accumulate consecutive `data:` lines and join with `\n` before JSON.parse, and tolerate stray `data:` prefixes. That would be a small change and unblock POC.

jamie_smith: customer asked about timeline — they want this fixed before end of quarter demo. Can we get a patch in next 48h?

rui_oncall: I can cut a hotfix branch to make the SDK parser more tolerant. akshat, do we need any config toggles on the server to reduce per-event size?

akshat_infra: We can add a temporary server-side throttle to cap event payloads to ~2KB and insert `:hb\n` heartbeat every 10s for the affected tenant. Requires a rollout to hosted routing layer and a short config flag. Low risk.

morgan_dev: plan: 1) SDK hotfix to tolerate split `data:` lines (PR today) 2) add tenant flag to emit smaller SSE chunks + heartbeats (deploy can be targeted to Valence only) 3) docs/guidance for customers behind aggressive proxies (recommended heartbeat and client buffering).

jamie_smith: I'll share the patch ETA with Valence and ask them to test SDK hotfix first. Also looping in legal for whether we can suggest bypassing proxy for the demo.

deploy-bot: [CI] SDK hotfix branch created: refs/heads/sse-tolerant-parser-valence (build queued) :gear:

morgan_dev: thanks. I'll open the PR and link to the repro instructions and the raw capture.

rui_oncall: follow-up items for oncall: monitor connection close codes for Valence tenant (1001/1006 spikes) and set an alert if 5+ truncation errors per minute. I'll add tracing on the gateway for partial-write detections.

jamie_smith: perfect. Valence is looped in and will test the SDK once PR build passes. I'll update here after first verification. :raised_hands:
